meta.purpose: Translate VA rating criteria into clinical questions for private providers
meta.philosophy: Doctors aren't lawyers. Ask medical questions, not legal ones.

MIGRAINES_SECONDARY.title: Medical Opinion Request: Migraine Headaches
MIGRAINES_SECONDARY.education_point: The VA rates migraines based on frequency of 'prostrating' attacks (requiring the patient to lie down in a dark room). The rating schedule distinguishes between 0%, 30%, and 50% based on attack frequency.

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Does the patient report headaches that require them to stop all activity and rest in a dark, quiet room? If so, please use the term 'prostrating' in your documentation if clinically accurate.
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: This term triggers higher ratings under 38 CFR § 4.124a, DC 8100

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Based on your treatment history, approximately how many prostrating attacks does the patient experience per month on average?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Frequency determines rating: <2/month=0%, 2+/month=30%, very frequent=50%

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: The patient has service-connected Tinnitus. Based on your medical knowledge, is it plausible that the chronic stress or sensory overload from tinnitus could aggravate or trigger migraines?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Establishes secondary service connection

nexus_language_options: The veteran's migraines are at least as likely as not aggravated by their service-connected tinnitus.
It is at least as likely as not that the veteran's migraine condition is secondary to their service-connected tinnitus.
The veteran's chronic tinnitus more likely than not contributes to the frequency and severity of their migraines.

PTSD_NON_COMBAT.title: Medical Opinion Request: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (Personal Trauma)
PTSD_NON_COMBAT.target_audience: Psychologist / Psychiatrist / Licensed Clinical Social Worker
PTSD_NON_COMBAT.education_point: For PTSD claims without combat stressors, the VA requires: (1) a confirmed stressor event, (2) current PTSD diagnosis per DSM-5, and (3) a medical nexus linking the stressor to current symptoms. The standard is 'at least as likely as not' (>50% probability).

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Does the patient meet DSM-5 criteria for PTSD (Criterion A stressor, B intrusion, C avoidance, D cognition/mood, E arousal)?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: VA requires formal DSM-5 diagnosis

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Please note if symptoms are distinct from other diagnoses (e.g., Adjustment Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder) or if PTSD is the primary diagnosis.
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: VA denies claims when PTSD isn't clearly differentiated

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Please describe how the condition affects occupational functioning, social relationships, and activities of daily living. Specific examples are helpful (e.g., 'Difficulty maintaining employment due to hypervigilance').
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Severity determines rating percentage (0-100%)

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: How long has the patient exhibited these symptoms? Are they chronic and persistent?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: VA requires evidence symptoms persist beyond adjustment period

nexus_language_options: It is at least as likely as not that the veteran's PTSD is related to their reported in-service stressor.
Based on my clinical evaluation and review of the veteran's history, the current PTSD symptoms are more likely than not connected to their military service trauma.
The veteran's PTSD diagnosis is at least as likely as not caused by the traumatic event that occurred during their military service.

SLEEP_APNEA_SECONDARY.title: Medical Opinion Request: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (Secondary to PTSD/Rhinitis)
SLEEP_APNEA_SECONDARY.target_audience: Sleep Medicine Specialist / Pulmonologist / Primary Care
SLEEP_APNEA_SECONDARY.education_point: Sleep apnea can be service-connected as secondary to other conditions (PTSD-related weight gain, rhinitis causing nasal obstruction, etc.). The VA requires sleep study results (AHI score) and a medical nexus.

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: What is the patient's Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) from their most recent sleep study? Does it meet diagnostic criteria for OSA?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: AHI >5 confirms diagnosis. AHI >20 supports higher ratings.

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Is CPAP or similar breathing assistance device medically required? Is the patient compliant with therapy?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: CPAP requirement = automatic 50% rating under VA rules

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: If the patient has PTSD: Is it medically plausible that PTSD-related factors (weight gain from psychotropic medications, hypervigilance disrupting sleep architecture, alcohol use for symptom management) contributed to their sleep apnea?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Establishes secondary connection to service-connected PTSD

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: If the patient has chronic rhinitis: Does nasal obstruction from rhinitis contribute to airway collapse during sleep?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Physical obstruction can establish direct secondary connection

nexus_language_options: It is at least as likely as not that the veteran's obstructive sleep apnea is secondary to (or aggravated by) their service-connected PTSD.
The veteran's sleep apnea is more likely than not caused or aggravated by their service-connected rhinitis.
Based on the temporal relationship and medical literature, the veteran's OSA is at least as likely as not related to weight gain from PTSD medications.

TINNITUS.title: Medical Opinion Request: Tinnitus
TINNITUS.education_point: Tinnitus is rated at 10% if recurrent (not constant tapping/clicking). The VA requires documentation that tinnitus exists and affects the veteran, plus a nexus to noise exposure during service.

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Does the patient report persistent ringing, buzzing, or other sounds in their ears? Is it constant or intermittent?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Recurrent tinnitus qualifies for 10% rating

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: How does the tinnitus affect the patient's daily life (sleep disturbance, concentration difficulties, emotional distress)?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Documents severity even though rating is fixed at 10%

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Based on the patient's reported military occupational specialty (MOS) and noise exposure history, is it medically plausible that their service caused or aggravated their tinnitus?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Establishes service connection

nexus_language_options: It is at least as likely as not that the veteran's tinnitus is related to noise exposure during military service.
The veteran's tinnitus is more likely than not caused by their documented acoustic trauma during service.
Based on the veteran's military occupational specialty and reported noise exposure, their tinnitus is at least as likely as not service-connected.

KNEE_PAIN_DIRECT.title: Medical Opinion Request: Knee Condition (Direct Service Connection)
KNEE_PAIN_DIRECT.target_audience: Orthopedic Surgeon / Sports Medicine / Primary Care
KNEE_PAIN_DIRECT.education_point: The VA rates knee conditions based on limitation of motion (flexion degrees), instability, and pain on use. X-rays showing degenerative changes support higher ratings.

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Please measure and document knee flexion in degrees. Normal is 0-140°. Note any limitation.
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Flexion to 45° = 30%, flexion to 15° = 40%, flexion <15° = 50%

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Is there ligamentous instability (ACL/PCL/MCL/LCL)? Does the knee give way during normal activities?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Instability adds to rating under separate diagnostic codes

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Does the patient experience pain with normal use? Is function limited by pain (e.g., difficulty climbing stairs, kneeling)?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Painful motion triggers 'pain on use' rating principle

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Based on the patient's reported injury history (e.g., airborne landing, vehicle accident during service), is it medically plausible that their current knee condition originated from that event?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Establishes direct service connection

nexus_language_options: It is at least as likely as not that the veteran's current knee condition is related to their documented in-service injury.
The veteran's knee pathology is more likely than not a result of the traumatic event that occurred during active duty service.
Based on the temporal relationship and mechanism of injury, the veteran's knee condition is at least as likely as not service-connected.

LUMBAR_STRAIN.title: Medical Opinion Request: Lumbar Spine Condition
LUMBAR_STRAIN.target_audience: Orthopedic Surgeon / Physiatrist / Chiropractor / Primary Care
LUMBAR_STRAIN.education_point: The VA rates spine conditions based on limitation of motion (forward flexion measured in degrees from vertical), incapacitating episodes, and functional impairment. Imaging showing degenerative changes supports the claim.

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Please measure lumbar forward flexion using goniometer or inclinometer (degrees from vertical). Normal is 90°. Document any limitation.
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: 30° or less = 40%, 60° or less = 20%, limited but >60° = 10%

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Does the patient experience episodes of acute back pain requiring bed rest or significant activity limitation? If so, approximately how many episodes per year?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Incapacitating episodes can increase rating to 60% (6+ weeks/year)

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: How does the back condition limit the patient's ability to work, perform household tasks, or engage in recreational activities?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Supports 'unemployability' claims and secondary conditions

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Based on the patient's military occupational history (heavy lifting, ruck marches, airborne operations), is it medically plausible that their service caused or permanently aggravated their lumbar condition?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Establishes service connection or aggravation

nexus_language_options: It is at least as likely as not that the veteran's lumbar spine condition is related to their military service activities.
The veteran's chronic back pain is more likely than not caused or permanently aggravated by the repetitive heavy lifting and physical demands of their military occupation.
Based on the veteran's service history and current pathology, their lumbar condition is at least as likely as not service-connected.

RHINITIS_PACT_ACT.title: Medical Opinion Request: Chronic Rhinitis (PACT Act Presumptive)
RHINITIS_PACT_ACT.education_point: Under the PACT Act, chronic rhinitis is a presumptive condition for veterans with qualifying service in Southwest Asia or other covered locations. No nexus statement is required IF service meets PACT Act criteria. However, diagnosis confirmation is needed.

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Does the patient have chronic rhinitis (inflammation of nasal passages lasting >12 weeks)? Please confirm diagnosis.
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Formal diagnosis triggers presumptive service connection

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: Please document symptoms: nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, post-nasal drip, facial pain/pressure. Are symptoms persistent or seasonal?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Severity affects rating percentage

required_verbiage.doctor_ask: What treatments have been tried (nasal sprays, antihistamines, etc.)? Is condition partially controlled or refractory?
required_verbiage.rating_relevance: Demonstrates chronicity and severity

nexus_language_options: The veteran has chronic rhinitis as defined by clinical criteria. (Note: If PACT Act service confirmed, no nexus statement needed.)
The patient's chronic rhinitis is documented and meets diagnostic criteria for presumptive service connection under the PACT Act.
